question: Nucleons are subatomic particles found inside the atom. They consist of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**protons and neutrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nucleons** are the subatomic particles that constitute the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The two types of nucleons are **protons** and **neutrons**, which are bound together by the **strong nuclear force**.
 
• **Protons** carry a positive charge (+1) and have a mass approximately equal to 1 atomic mass unit (amu).
 
• **Neutrons** are electrically neutral particles with a mass similar to that of protons (approximately 1 amu).
 
• Electrons are not considered nucleons because they are located outside the nucleus and have negligible mass compared to protons and neutrons.
 
• The nucleus is responsible for most of the atom's mass, as protons and neutrons are significantly heavier than electrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protons:**

 
 
• Protons are positively charged particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The number of protons in an atom defines its **atomic number**, which determines the element's identity.
 
• Protons are composed of three quarks (two up quarks and one down quark) held together by the strong nuclear force.
 
 
 
• **Neutrons:**
 
 
• Neutrons are neutral particles that also reside in the atomic nucleus.
 
• They play a crucial role in stabilizing the nucleus by reducing the repulsive forces between positively charged protons.
 
• Neutrons consist of three quarks (one up quark and two down quarks) bound by the strong nuclear force.
 
 
 
• **Electrons:**
 
 
• Electrons are negatively charged particles that orbit the nucleus in specific energy levels or shells.
 
• Their mass is approximately 1/1836 of a proton, making their contribution to the atom's total mass negligible.
 
• Electrons are not nucleons because they are not part of the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Strong Nuclear Force:**
 
 
• The strong nuclear force is the fundamental interaction responsible for binding protons and neutrons together in the nucleus.
 
• It operates over very short distances (approximately 1 femtometer) and is the strongest force in nature.
 
• This force overcomes the electrostatic repulsion between positively charged protons in the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding nucleons is critical in fields like nuclear physics, radiology, and energy production.
 
• Nuclear reactions, such as fission and fusion, involve changes in the arrangement of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
 
• Isotopes of an element differ in their number of neutrons and have applications in medicine, dating techniques, and scientific research.
